{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|Cuisine of the United Kingdom]] | [[Cookbook:Dessert|Dessert]] | [[Cookbook:Rhubarb|Rhubarb]]

'''Rhubarb crumble''' is a traditional [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United Kingdom|British]] [[Cookbook:Dessert|dessert]]. Served traditionally with [[Cookbook:Custard|custard]] (though you can of course serve with [[Cookbook:Cream|cream]] or [[Cookbook:Vanilla Ice Cream|ice cream]]) it is a hearty, filling, and warm feast, best served after a light meal. This version has a flour-based crumble topping, it and simply uses rhubarb and sugar as the filling (unlike the cornstarch etc. in other versions). The rhubarb juice acts as a sufficient sauce.

== Ingredients ==
*400 [[Cookbook:Gram|g]] (1 ¾ [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] or 14 [[Cookbook:Ounce|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Rhubarb|rhubarb]], cut into pieces roughly 1.5 [[Cookbook:Centimetre (cm)|cm]] long (no need to be consistent)
*15 g (2 [[Cookbook:Tablespoon|tbsp]]) light [[Cookbook:Sugar|brown sugar]]
*75 g (2 ½ [[Cookbook:Oz|oz]]) [[Cookbook:Butter|butter]] or [[Cookbook:Margarine|margarine]], cut in pieces
*100 g (3 ½ oz) [[Cookbook:Flour|plain flour]]
*50 g (1 ¾ oz) [[Cookbook:Flour|wholemeal flour]]
*50 g (1 ¾ oz) white granulated [[Cookbook:Sugar|sugar]]
*1 [[Cookbook:Pinch|pinch]] [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] (optional)

== Procedure ==
#Preheat the [[Cookbook:Oven|oven]] to 200°C (180°C fan).
#Rinse and drain the rhubarb pieces, and place them in a deep [[Cookbook:Baking Dish|ovenproof dish]]. Add the light brown sugar and mix briefly.
#Put the flours in a mixing bowl. Add the butter. With your fingers (not the palms of your hands), rub the butter into the flour until it resembles breadcrumbs.
#Sprinkle the sugar and cinnamon over this mixture, and mix them in briefly.
#Sprinkle the crumble mixture over the fruit, making a complete layer. Do not press the topping down—you want it light and crumbly.
#Put the dish in the oven (no lid) for 35–45 minutes until crisp and a bit brown.
#Serve with custard.
